data.name: General LLM reasoning without external tools

notes.text: This page defines a high-end complexity scale for general LLM reasoning without external tools: no theorem prover, no code execution, no search engine, no Lean, no brute-force construction search.

The baseline is the reported OpenAI result on the Erdős unit-distance conjecture: an internal general-purpose reasoning model generated a counterexample to a long-standing conjecture in discrete geometry. OpenAI says the result came from a general-purpose reasoning model rather than a system trained specifically for mathematics or scaffolded to search proof strategies. The companion remarks paper says the proof was “first mathematically generated in one shot” by an internal OpenAI model, then refined expositionally with human/Codex interaction.
Sources: OpenAI announcement; Alon–Bloom–Gowers–Litt–Sawin–Shankar–Tsimerman–Wang–Wood companion remarks.

If Level 1 is real for pure/general LLM reasoning, then the core question becomes whether Levels 2–8 scale smoothly, or whether there is a hard wall around Levels 8–9 where “taste”, framework invention, and theory construction become qualitatively different.

sections.title: The 12-level scale
sections.rationale: One card per level, carrying the complexity definition, illustrative target, and generalized-science implication.

data.name: Level 1 — Famous-conjecture counterexample
data.definition: Finds a valid counterexample to a long-standing conjecture.
data.authorityScope: Baseline: original research discovery, not benchmark math.

notes.text: Example open problems / target classes: Erdős unit-distance style extremal-combinatorics counterexample.
If generalized beyond mathematics, this opens up: Finding flaws in accepted models; discovering overlooked mechanisms in biology, economics, materials, and climate science.

data.name: Level 2 — Deep-synthesis counterexample
data.definition: Finds a counterexample using several distant mathematical ideas.
data.authorityScope: Requires fusing remote concepts, not one local trick.

notes.text: Example open problems / target classes: Hadwiger–Nelson variants; Borsuk-type variants; geometric Ramsey counterexamples.
If generalized beyond mathematics, this opens up: Unexpected bridges between fields: ecology into economics, condensed matter into neuroscience, information theory into medicine.

data.name: Level 3 — New theorem proof
data.definition: Proves a previously open theorem in a narrow research area.
data.authorityScope: A proof must close every logical gap.

notes.text: Example open problems / target classes: Erdős–Straus conjecture; Casas-Alvero conjecture; narrow algebraic/combinatorial cases.
If generalized beyond mathematics, this opens up: Solving well-defined scientific questions where the ingredients already exist but were not connected correctly.

data.name: Level 4 — Hidden-lemma chain
data.definition: Invents several intermediate lemmas not obvious from the statement.
data.authorityScope: Requires proof architecture, not just final-step insight.

notes.text: Example open problems / target classes: Union-closed sets conjecture; lonely runner conjecture; graph reconstruction conjecture.
If generalized beyond mathematics, this opens up: Discovery of missing intermediate mechanisms in gene networks, disease pathways, cognition, climate, or complex systems.

data.name: Level 5 — Long publishable proof
data.definition: Produces a paper-level proof that survives expert review.

notes.text: Example open problems / target classes: Restricted Jacobian conjecture cases; Kaplansky-style algebra conjectures.
If generalized beyond mathematics, this opens up: End-to-end scientific explanations spanning hundreds of interacting factors: whole-cell models, aging mechanisms, causal climate models.

data.name: Level 6 — Cross-field proof
data.definition: Solves a problem by importing machinery from another field.
data.authorityScope: Requires recognizing bridges between mathematical languages.

notes.text: Example open problems / target classes: Collatz-style dynamics via ergodic theory; combinatorics via algebraic geometry.
If generalized beyond mathematics, this opens up: True interdisciplinary breakthroughs where one field unlocks another.

data.name: Level 7 — Multiple related open problems
data.definition: Solves a cluster of connected problems.
data.authorityScope: Shows a general mechanism, not a one-off solution.

notes.text: Example open problems / target classes: A family of Erdős problems; connected extremal graph conjectures.
If generalized beyond mathematics, this opens up: Solving whole classes of scientific puzzles at once rather than isolated cases.

data.name: Level 8 — New method
data.definition: Creates a reusable proof technique or construction method.
data.authorityScope: The output becomes a tool for future mathematics.

notes.text: Example open problems / target classes: New sieve method; new probabilistic construction; new algebraic encoding.
If generalized beyond mathematics, this opens up: New experimental, computational, or theoretical methods used by thousands of researchers.

data.name: Level 9 — New framework
data.definition: Invents definitions or abstractions that reorganize a subfield.
data.authorityScope: Changes the representation of the problem space.

notes.text: Example open problems / target classes: New framework for additive combinatorics, higher-dimensional expanders, categorical probability.
If generalized beyond mathematics, this opens up: New paradigms comparable in role to evolutionary theory, information theory, plate tectonics, or game theory.

data.name: Level 10 — Theory-building sequence
data.definition: Produces definitions, lemmas, theorems, examples, applications.
data.authorityScope: Requires sustained mathematical taste and direction.

notes.text: Example open problems / target classes: A full theory around a new invariant, graph limit object, cohomology theory, or proof calculus.
If generalized beyond mathematics, this opens up: Autonomous research programs producing years of coherent scientific progress.

data.name: Level 11 — Major central conjecture
data.authorityScope: Must overcome many deep failed approaches.

notes.text: Example open problems / target classes: Riemann Hypothesis; P vs NP; Hodge; Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer; Navier–Stokes; Yang–Mills.
If generalized beyond mathematics, this opens up: Progress on civilization-scale bottlenecks: fusion theory, room-temperature superconductivity theory, aging, consciousness, climate control.

data.name: Level 12 — Field creation
data.definition: Creates a new mathematical language or domain.
data.authorityScope: Expands what mathematics can naturally express.

notes.text: Example open problems / target classes: Something comparable in role to category theory, scheme theory, forcing, or homotopy type theory.
If generalized beyond mathematics, this opens up: Entirely new sciences or conceptual languages humans had not yet formulated.
